summary: A report on the March 1972 meeting at MIT where Vint Cerf and colleagues formed the Network Measurement Group to plan measurement experiments on the ARPANET. The group agreed to set aside a range of links, 159 through 191, for measurement traffic. Some links were for a host discard service, and others were for traffic statistics sent by the IMPs.

plainLanguage.summary: This report describes a meeting to plan measurements of the ARPANET and its hosts. Participants set aside links for measurement traffic and discussed shared statistics, host surveys and traffic generators.

sections.title: Forming the Measurement Group
sections.content: On March 17, 1972, a group met at MIT project MAC to discuss existing and planned measurements of network and host behavior. Vint Cerf of UCLA/NMC chaired the Network Measurement Group (NMG). RFC 323 records the discussions and agreements.
sections.plainLanguage: Researchers met to coordinate ways to measure the network and the computers connected to it. Vint Cerf chaired the group.

sections.title: Links Allocated for Measurement
sections.content:
The group allocated links 159 through 191 for network measurement. Links 159 through 174 were designated HOST DISCARD: cooperating hosts would discard messages on them without sending an error. Links 175 through 190 could be assigned as needed by Vint Cerf, and link 191 was for IMPs to send measurement traffic based on their statistics.

A separate process-discard service was suggested, but no socket number was proposed until a survey of socket use at hosts had been completed.
sections.plainLanguage: The group set aside a range of links for measurement. Some were for messages that hosts would discard, and one was for traffic reporting IMP measurements.

sections.title: NCP Statistics and Reporting
sections.content:
The Network Working Group agreed on a minimal NCP measurement procedure for a standard 24-hour period. Each host would count bits and messages sent and received for each other host, with average round-trip delay as an optional measure. The counts exclude measurement links, experimental NCP links and link 0.

A process on a socket number yet to be specified would provide the last sample period's statistics. The report begins with a day number and start time in minutes, followed by a format byte that indicates which kinds of statistics are included.
sections.plainLanguage: Each host would keep a daily count of traffic sent and received. It could also report average round-trip delay and provide the results in a shared format.

sections.title: Other Measurement Proposals
sections.content:
The report discusses measuring connection capacity, transmission delay, mean time between failures and availability. It also describes host-survey programs that periodically checked host status, proposals to measure file transfers and interest in artificial traffic generators for testing network capacity.

The report gives examples of existing work at several sites, but presents the traffic generators and many measurement ideas as ongoing or proposed efforts.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants also discussed checking which hosts were available, measuring file transfers and generating test traffic. These were reported as experiments and proposals.
